== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|The [[Subspace]] [[Drive]] is a critical propulsion technology used for long-distance transportation, as traveling through the dimension of [[Subspace]] is considered the only way to achieve accurate movement across vast distances. The drive functions by creating a warp or tear in reality, allowing vessels to perform a "dive" into [[Subspace]]. These maneuvers vary in scale from micro-dives, which only skim the surface of the dimension, to standard or long-distance dives. While [[Subspace]] itself is potentially infinite, travel is limited by practical factors such as fuel consumption and the stability of the drive. Technological variations of the drive exist, ranging from massive cores housed in large docking rooms to small internal versions integrated into individuals. Some advanced iterations, such as the [[Aether Drive]], are powered by magic. The drive's operation carries significant risks; improper use or damage can lead to an immediate drive rupture. Additionally, the process of diving pulls surrounding matter into [[Subspace]], which can create violent storms and place extreme physical strain on the vessel. Beyond its mechanical function, the drive interacts with the environment in unique ways. [[Subspace]] creatures are attracted to the drives, seeking them out as a source of nourishment. Furthermore, certain entities can experience "[[Subspace madness]]" due to the patterns visible during travel. The effectiveness and navigation of these drives can be enhanced by a [[Pilot]], whose presence can evolve the technology to reach legendary levels of speed and efficiency.}}

== The Captain ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-01-the-captain|The [[Subspace]] [[Drive]] is a starship component consisting of a large, twisting, and semi-transparent tube core that allows vessels to enter [[Subspace]]. While routing power to the device can cause an instant rupture and [[binding]]-spells are capable of striking it, the drive can also be delayed from a distance. Although the narrator's ship lacks this technology, the vessel known as [[Horizon]] utilizes a default version that remains stuck without a [[Pilot]]. Through the evolution provided by a [[Pilot]]'s gifts, the drive can be restored to peace and order, allowing [[Horizon]] to regain its legendary heights. Ultimately, the [[The Last Horizon|Last Horizon]] also utilizes a [[Subspace]] [[Drive]] for its operations.}}

== The Engineer ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-02-the-engineer|As a vital component of the envisioned fleet, [[Subspace Drives]] facilitate interstellar travel, though they can trigger various warning alarms during operation. The vessel known as [[The Last Horizon]] utilizes such a drive, but it suffers from malfunctions and requires repairs. This specific unit is particularly unreliable, possessing only a fourteen percent chance of reaching [[Subspace]] without experiencing a rupture. While the [[Starhammer]] contains an internal drive that is less efficient than those found on real starships, all such drives face challenges when diving into [[Subspace]] within a planet's atmosphere. Furthermore, the process of diving into [[Subspace]] causes surrounding matter to be pulled along with the ship.}}

<div class="wv-facts mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"><div class="wv-facts-head mw-collapsible-toggle">Sourced facts <span class="wv-facts-count">9</span></div>

== The Pilot ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|A [[Subspace]] [[Drive]] is a mechanism utilized to facilitate travel through subspace. During the events involving the Vallenar ship, the drive was employed to undock and begin its departure. Within the [[Karoshan]] facility, isolated cores of these drives exist with the potential to rupture should a dimensional breach occur. The crew later relied on a [[Subspace]] [[Drive]] to conduct a retreat, though it was noted that the drive would fail if [[Omega]] tried to travel too far through the [[Subspace lock]].}}

<li>{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|The [[Karoshan]] facility contains isolated [[Subspace Drive]] cores that can rupture in case of a dimensional breach.<ref name="lh-04-the-pilot-c20">''The Pilot'', chapter 20</ref>}}</li>
